subject: POC capacity planning / next steps - Redwood POC for Acme AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & POC plan — Redwood x Acme AI

Thanks for the call earlier, Sam — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC:

Summary of goals / success criteria:
- End-to-end latency below 250ms 95th percentile for single-request flows (user messages avg 120 tokens)
- Stable throughput of ~120 qps sustained for 30-minute windows during peak scenarios
- Cost target: <$0.015 per 1k tokens inferred for serving layer (measured in our dashboard)
- Clear functional pass: conversation integrity, tool-calling correctness, and no model regressions vs your baseline prompts

Evaluation plan & timelines:
- Week 1 (Apr 6–10): Environment provisioning, sample dataset ingest, baseline runs
- Week 2 (Apr 13–17): Load testing and tuning (autoscale + batching), run eval prompts and collect metrics
- Week 3 (Apr 20–24): Final validation with stakeholder signoffs and handoff to CloudOps for prod runbook

Ownership:
- Redwood AE (me) — program manager, customer liaison, contract/SOW
- Redwood SE (Rishi) — infra sizing, load tests, on-call for run validation
- Acme CloudOps (Sam) — integration, network access, procurement coordination

Capacity planning notes (initial ask):
- We propose reserved capacity of 4 x A100-class GPUs for the POC baseline with autoscaling up to 8 GPUs for bursts. Rishi will confirm exact instance types and expected concurrency based on your prompt lengths.
- Warm pool: we recommend a 1–2 GPU warm pool to keep cold-start latency down during scale events.
- KV / prefix cache: we will prewarm with your 10k sample prefixes to reduce token generation cost and latency.

Attachments: attached is a short POC MA plan (redwood_poc_ma_plan.pdf) and a capacity estimate sheet (capacity_estimate_acme.xlsx). Please review the success criteria and let us know if anything should be adjusted.

Next steps:
1) Sam: confirm procurement contact and any required PO template by EOD Friday (Apr 3)
2) Rishi/Vivek/Marissa: finalize instance sizing and SOW draft by Apr 5
3) Kickoff meeting tentatively: Apr 6 (30–45 min)

Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — that all looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications:
- Success criteria: Can we add a Spike/Recovery criterion for autoscale? Specifically: after a synthetic 5x traffic spike, system should return to baseline scale within 10 minutes without error rate >1%.
- Cost target: we will measure both token unit cost and end-to-end infra cost (to include networking egress). Can you include an example of how you report infra cost per token?

Procurement: looping in procurement. Hi — we will need your standard SOW and a non-disclosure addendum for our legal team. We generally require net 30 payment terms for POCs and a short pre-PO form; happy to share.

Sam

Thanks — added a couple technical details so CloudOps has something concrete to review.

Capacity / sizing assumptions (initial):
- Baseline reserved capacity: 4 x A100 (40GB) equivalent GPUs
  - Expected sustained concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions (avg 120 tokens/user) with continuous KV cache enabled
  - Expected throughput: ~120 qps (as Marissa called out) at p95 latency ~210–240ms with batching tuned for 8–12 requests per batch
- Autoscale policy: scale steps of +2 GPUs, cooldown 3 minutes, max burst to 8 GPUs. We maintain a warm pool of 1 GPU that is always available to keep cold-starts <100ms for new instances.
- Burst expectations: 5x traffic spike tolerance with automatic scale and graceful degradation: priority routing to reserved instances, then burst pool; fall back to smaller model variant if we hit max capacity
- Network: recommend peering; estimate egress during peak synthetic tests ~1.2 Gbps for full load (detailed calc in capacity_estimate_acme.xlsx)

Operational notes:
- We will instrument per-token cost and per-route latency in the Redwood Console and share dashboards. Sample dashboard link in the sheet.
- For the POC we can enable short-term extra logging retention (30 days) if you need traces for evaluation; extra retention beyond default will be an add-on.

Attachments: brief capacity worksheet (capacity_estimate_acme.xlsx) with assumptions and per-hour cost estimates.

I can join the kickoff on Apr 6 to run through the load-testing plan.
